Description
-----------

[![@yacinehmito](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6893840?u=f134c03dd80762d6c73a0f841ecd46b36329362c&v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/yacinehmito)

[yacinehmito](https://github.com/yacinehmito)

opened [on Aug 24, 2025](https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/30509#issue-3349639275)

Issue body actions

Version: Tested on 2.4.3 and latest main (ref [6314c3c](https://github.com/denoland/deno/commit/6314c3c46d04727a3c4483101813be57dcca2d8e)
)

Complex scenarios with symlinks in `node_modules` (such as those produced by `pnpm`) would work fine with `deno run` but break with `deno compile`, as the latter would be unable to resolve some modules.

My guess is that `deno compile` is unable to include in its VFS multiple symlinks with the same target. To be confirmed.

I produced a minimal example with explanations in this repository: [https://github.com/yacinehmito/mre-denoland-deno-30509](https://github.com/yacinehmito/mre-denoland-deno-30509)

Note that this breaks using `deno compile` with `"nodeModulesDir": "manual"` when installing dependencies with `pnpm` under the default `nodeLinker` (which is `isolated`).

Unrelated to this issue: In my particular project `deno compile` is also broken when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` (mimics the behavior of `npm`) but I did not manage to produce a minimal example yet.

Reactions are currently unavailable
